record.issue_text: The outbound credential-sync POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (refreshOAuthTokens.ts:11-17) sends only `calcomUserId` + `appSlug` with no authentication or secret header; `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is only used on the inbound webhook, so the parent app cannot verify the caller and anyone who learns the URL can request live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary user IDs/app slugs

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no authentication material (no secret header/body param, no HMAC, no Authorization header). In the same diff, `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is only checked on the *inbound* webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) and is not used for outbound credential-sync requests. This creates a concrete security gap: the parent app has no built-in way (from Cal.com’s request) to verify the caller, so if the sync endpoint is reachable and returns refreshed access tokens based on `calcomUserId`/`appSlug` as suggested by comments, the endpoint would be trivially callable by anyone who knows the URL unless the parent app adds its own auth out-of-band.
